findings.summary: The delivered Reservation lifecycle diverges from the frozen DOMAIN_CATALOG: the catalog-named state word 'released' does not exist anywhere in the delivered vocabulary, and the reservation graph's edges do not match the catalog chain.
findings.location: packages/domain/src/logistics_domain/states.py:794-801 (reservation graph), states.py EntityState union (~lines 312-398, no RELEASED member); authority: docs/architecture/DOMAIN_CATALOG.md:54 auxiliary prose 'Reservation(held→committed→released/expired)'.
findings.expected: Per the catalog chain: a 'released' lifecycle state exists; edges held→committed, committed→released, committed→expired.
findings.actual: EntityState has no RELEASED member (the union over all graphs, asserted 69 states, contains no 'released'); the reservation graph is held→{committed, cancelled, expired}, committed→{cancelled}; committed→released and committed→expired are absent; the extra edges held→expired, held→cancelled and committed→cancelled are not granted by the catalog prose.
findings.trigger: Any consumer expressing a released reservation, or any comparison of LIFECYCLE_TRANSITIONS with the catalog auxiliary section (this round's independent probe, log 21, checks 'LC all catalog chain edges...' and 'LC reservation held->committed->released/expired').
findings.observable_impact: The G02 phase criterion '32 entities and auxiliary records are expressible' cannot express a released reservation; P03-04 (version CAS / resource reservation storage) and the reservation APIs of P05/P16 inherit a vocabulary that conflates an operational release with a cancellation.
